title: Warmup Web Server
scenario: A small company left a training web server misconfigured. Explore this completely simulated target to find its hidden flag — no real network is ever contacted.

tasks.prompt: Scan the target. Which open ports do you see? Enter them separated by a comma.
tasks.hint1: Start by asking the simulated terminal to scan target.thm.
tasks.hint2: Try: nmap target.thm — the output lists 21 and 80.

tasks.prompt: What service is running on port 21?
tasks.hint1: Read the SERVICE column from the scan results.

tasks.prompt: What service is running on port 80?
tasks.hint1: Read the second open port in the simulated scan.
tasks.hint2: Port 80 is HTTP, the web service.

tasks.prompt: Find and submit the flag stored on the anonymous FTP server.
tasks.hint1: FTP is a way of transferring files. Connect with ftp target.thm, then sign in as anonymous.
tasks.hint2: After connecting, use ls to list files and cat flag.txt to read the flag.

learn.title: Why anonymous FTP is risky
learn.body: FTP means File Transfer Protocol: an older way to move files. Anonymous access lets anyone browse files without a personal account. On a real company system, that can accidentally expose sensitive documents — so public access should be disabled unless it is truly needed.
